name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~2%
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Griffith's incumbency and massive fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win at just 2% all point to a safe Republican hold; Powers' modest $85k war chest offers no path to competitiveness.
model.watch: A major scandal or Griffith retirement would be the only realistic opening, and even then the district's lean would keep Republicans favored.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan Griffith seeks another term in a southwestern Virginia district that leans Republican by about 22 points. He has raised over $1.8 million and holds nearly a million dollars on hand, while Democrat Joy Powers has raised about $85,000 with under $15,000 available. No outside groups are spending meaningfully in the race, and no public general-election polls are available.

Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 2% chance of an upset, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The Democratic environment nationally is somewhat favorable, but the margin of the lean and the resource gap make this a safe Republican seat. The main uncertainty is the usual tail risk of an unforeseen event, not any measurable Democratic strength.
